calls.summary: Marcus Reyes called about utility-scale solar electrical scope for a West Texas site and asked for a design-build quote. Oscar walked him through DC and MV collection tie-ins and booked a preconstruction consultation for the following week. Marcus confirmed the site details and left satisfied.

Danielle Cho requested a structured cabling estimate for a new DFW office fit-out, including Cat6 and fiber runs. Lila reviewed drop counts and scheduled a design consultation with the low-voltage team. The call ended with a confirmed on-site walkthrough.

Anthony Grubbs checked on the status of a medium voltage installation already underway at his industrial campus. Rosey pulled the project schedule and confirmed the substation tie-in date. He was reassured and no new work was booked.

Priya Nandakumar called as a new prospect to schedule a consultation for a medium voltage distribution project at a data center in Midlothian. Lee collected her company name, site address, timeline, and scope details, then booked a preconstruction consultation. She confirmed the appointment and asked for a follow-up email.

Greg Salazar wanted a quote for an industrial HVAC build with rooftop units and controls for a manufacturing plant. Mary gathered square footage and mechanical requirements and scheduled a site consultation. He agreed to the visit and shared his facility hours.

Tania Ford reported an after-hours electrical fault and asked for emergency service at her healthcare facility. Sue confirmed the 24/7 dispatch and gave an arrival window for the on-call technician. The call was a service dispatch, not a new consultation.

Roland Beck called to set up a preventative maintenance program for his mechanical systems across two buildings. Mike reviewed the inspection schedule and reporting options and booked a consultation to finalize the contract. Roland confirmed the meeting time.

Helen Ostrander disputed a charge on her latest invoice for completed electrical work. Jennifer reviewed the line items and opened a billing review ticket. Helen remained frustrated but agreed to wait for the adjustment.

Victor Almanza asked about a corporate interiors tenant improvement build-out including lighting and low-voltage. Rose captured the scope and booked a design consultation for his office suite. He confirmed availability for the walkthrough.

Karen Delgado called about a warranty issue on a recent structured cabling termination that failed testing. Oscar logged the defect and arranged a technician re-inspection. No new project was scheduled.

Brandon Pike raised an installation issue with inverter tie-ins on his solar collection scope that were behind schedule. Lila explained the crew reassignment and updated timeline. Brandon stayed unhappy about the delay and no consultation was booked.

Denise Whitaker called to cancel a scheduled maintenance visit for her mechanical equipment. Lee processed the cancellation and noted the account for follow-up. She declined to reschedule at this time.

Curtis Mabry complained that an emergency repair crew arrived later than the promised window at his plant. Mary apologized and escalated the dispatch complaint to the service manager. Curtis remained dissatisfied and the call closed without new work.

Sandra Pruitt left a voicemail asking someone to call her back about a pending change order on her electrical scope. The message rolled to voicemail after hours and no agent answered. A callback was queued for the next business day.

Leon Barrett angrily disputed a final invoice and threatened to withhold payment on a completed project. Jennifer tried to explain the retention terms but he refused to discuss further. The call ended unresolved with a manager escalation.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: The caller operates an advanced manufacturing facility with aging electrical distribution and wants to assess whether a full system upgrade is feasible without extended downtime. The caller mentioned potential plans for facility expansion in the next 18 months.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects a professional site assessment within two weeks and a detailed design proposal with cost and timeline. They want CEC to help determine whether a phased approach or a complete replacement makes sense for their operation.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus could have captured the facility email address for follow-up documentation and confirmed the expected duration and scope of the initial site visit so the caller could plan accordingly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling CEC Companies. This is Marcus Bell. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. My name is Jennifer Huang. We operate an advanced manufacturing facility outside Dallas, and I think we need to look at our electrical infrastructure. We have been getting some concerns about our power distribution.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Jennifer, thank you for calling. I am glad you reached out to us. So you are looking at your electrical infrastructure. Can you tell me a bit more about what specifically you are concerned about?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We have three production lines, and over the past few months we have noticed some voltage fluctuations. Our facility manager thinks we may need medium-voltage upgrades or possibly a complete system assessment. We are not sure where to start.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That makes sense. Medium-voltage assessment and upgrades are something we do all the time for industrial operations. Just to confirm, you are looking for a comprehensive evaluation of your electrical distribution, correct?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. We want a professional assessment. We are also planning for some expansion in the next year and a half, so we need to know if the current system can handle it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. So we will want to do a design and preconstruction assessment, including load studies and recommendations for your expansion. Let me get your facility address so I can make sure we have the right service team. What is your ZIP code?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We are at 75243, which is south of downtown Dallas.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. 75243 is in our primary service area. Now let me get your direct phone number so our project coordinator can reach you.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It is ****-****-****. That is my direct line.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. I have that. And what is the best email address for us to send documentation and the site visit confirmation?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Actually, just use my phone number for now. I check calls more regularly than email.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Understood. Jennifer, I am going to get you on our calendar for a site visit on Wednesday of next week. Our engineer will bring diagnostic equipment and walk through all three production lines with your facility manager. You can expect that visit to take about two to three hours. Does Wednesday work for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, Wednesday works. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great. You will receive a confirmation text at that number. Our team is really looking forward to working with you on this project. If you have any questions before Wednesday, please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you for choosing CEC Companies, Jennifer.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Huang, facilities manager for an advanced manufacturing operation in south Dallas, called to schedule a professional electrical infrastructure assessment. Her facility has experienced voltage fluctuations across three production lines and is planning expansion within 18 months. Marcus Bell captured her name, ZIP code, phone number, and scheduled a two-hour site visit for the following Wednesday with CEC's engineering team. The call was professional and efficient, though Marcus did not secure an email address as requested by protocol.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, you handled the qualification and scheduling really well on this new-customer intake. Your tone was confident and you clearly explained what the site visit would involve, which set good expectations. One thing: when Jennifer hesitated on the email, you accepted it without gently re-emphasizing why we need it for documentation and follow-up. Next time, try something like, "I understand. What I will do is send a quick confirmation text with the date and time, and we can add your email to our notes for the formal proposal after the visit. That way you are covered either way." Also, consider asking one warm question about their current maintenance program or what contractor they have worked with before. It builds rapport and gives us intelligence for the proposal. Great call overall.

transcript.text: Thank you for calling CEC Companies, this is Marcus in our commercial solutions team. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, my name is Dana Whitfield. I'm the facilities director for a new distribution center we're building out near Midlothian, and I'm trying to find a contractor for the electrical and low-voltage work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great to meet you, Dana. Congratulations on the new facility. Can you tell me a bit about the scope? Square footage, and whether you need power distribution, structured cabling, or both?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's about 180,000 square feet. We definitely need the building power distribution, and then Cat6 and fiber drops throughout the office and warehouse floor. There may be some medium-voltage tie-in too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. That's right in our wheelhouse. CEC offers a design-build approach, so we can handle the commercial electrical installation, the medium-voltage distribution, and the structured cabling all under one roof, coordinated through our BIM team.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That sounds good, but honestly I want to keep this manageable. For the cabling side, what does that usually run per drop?
highlights: what does that usually run per drop

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Completely fair question. Structured cabling typically lands between 150 and 300 dollars per drop depending on Cat6 versus fiber and the terminations. Once our estimators see the drawings we'll give you a firm bid, no surprises.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay. I'll be upfront, I'm getting a couple of quotes on this. There's a smaller outfit here in town that bid the electrical, but they don't really touch the medium-voltage work.
highlights: I'm getting a couple of quotes
they don't really touch the medium-voltage work

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a common gap, Dana. The advantage of CEC is that our medium-voltage crews, our electrical teams, and our cabling technicians are all in-house, so you're not stitching together three vendors when the schedule gets tight. That coordination usually saves time and rework.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That matters, because we've got a hard occupancy date in September and I can't slip it. One more thing, would you also be able to handle the AV in the conference rooms?
highlights: handle the AV in the conference rooms

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. Our AV Solutions group does displays, conferencing, and control systems, so we can fold that right into the same design package. And a September occupancy is very achievable if we start preconstruction now.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Alright, that's encouraging. I don't want to get locked into anything huge before I see numbers, though.
highlights: don't want to get locked into anything huge

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You won't be. The next step is just a no-obligation consultation where our preconstruction engineer reviews your drawings and walks the site. Would Thursday at 10 AM work for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 works. Let me give you my email so you can send the details.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, I've got you down for Thursday at 10 AM with our preconstruction team. What's the best email and cell for you, Dana?
highlights: got you down for Thursday at 10 AM

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's dana.whitfield@ridgelinelogistics.com, and my cell is 214-555-0148.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. You'll receive a confirmation shortly. Thanks for calling CEC, Dana, we look forward to building great things with you.

transcript.text: Hi there. Thanks for reaching out to CEC Companies. This is Marcus from our commercial contracting team. Are you calling about a specific project or service need today?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. Yes, we're looking at upgrading the electrical infrastructure at our manufacturing facility in the Dallas area. We've outgrown our current capacity.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, that's exactly what we specialize in. I'd love to help you explore options. Can you tell me roughly how many square feet we're talking about for your facility?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: About 120,000 square feet. We need more power distribution and some updates to our control systems.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. A 120k sq ft manufacturing site with power distribution and controls is definitely in our wheelhouse. Are you looking to expand capacity, upgrade to newer equipment, or both?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Both, actually. We want to add some new production lines and modernize what we have.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. That sounds like a design-build opportunity where we can assess your current infrastructure and plan the upgrades. Have you worked with design-build contractors before, or would this be your first time?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: First time. We want to make sure everything is coordinated properly and done right.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Smart approach. That's exactly what design-build does, best practice here in the Dallas market. I'd like to schedule a free consultation with one of our project managers to do a site walk and understand your timeline and budget range. Would next Tuesday the 18th work for you, maybe around 2 PM?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Tuesday at 2 works for me. What do I need to prepare?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Just have your facility key available and maybe a sketch of where the new production lines will go if you have one. We'll bring a BIM specialist to take measurements and photos. Your consultation is booked for Tuesday, March 18th at 2 PM. You'll get a reminder text the day before. Any questions?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No, sounds good. Thanks, Marcus.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. We're excited to help. If anything comes up, call us at 877-936-2933. See you Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for calling CEC Companies. This is Marcus. How can we help you build something great today?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. Yeah, I'm calling because we've got a data center facility in the Dallas area and we need to upgrade our electrical infrastructure. We're looking at medium voltage installation and maybe some other MEP work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's fantastic. We work with a lot of mission critical facilities like data centers. Just to get a better picture, is this a new facility or an existing one that needs upgrades?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: It's an existing facility. We built it about three years ago but we're expanding and need to handle a lot more power capacity.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. So you're looking at expansion work. When you think about the timeline, are you looking to get this done in the next few months or is this more of a longer term planning phase?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: We'd like to start within the next two months if possible. We've got some growth projections that are pushing us to move on this.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. That's a realistic timeline for a scope like that. Have you worked with a design build contractor before or would you need help from the design phase all the way through construction?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: We'd probably want the full design build approach. We've got some in house engineering but we'd rather have a single point of responsibility.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That makes sense. CEC can definitely handle that end to end. transcript.speaker: consumer

qaPairs.question: What trades does CEC self-perform?
qaPairs.answer: CEC self-performs electrical, mechanical, and low-voltage technology work for commercial and industrial projects. I'd love to set up a consultation with a specialist to scope your project.

qaPairs.question: Do you handle design-build projects?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Design and Preconstruction team delivers full lifecycle design-to-delivery with BIM and Trimble coordination. Let's book a consultation to review your project goals.

qaPairs.question: Can you install medium-voltage distribution?
qaPairs.answer: Absolutely, we install medium-voltage cable, terminations, and substation tie-ins for large sites. A specialist can walk through your requirements on a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you do utility-scale solar work?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we handle DC collection, MV collection, and inverter and substation tie-ins for utility-scale solar, including 400-plus MW deployments in West Texas. I can schedule a consultation to discuss your solar scope.

qaPairs.question: Do you serve data centers?
qaPairs.answer: We provide mission-critical MEP solutions, including work like the 260,000 square foot MDN HUB Data Center in Midlothian. Let's set up a consultation with our mission-critical team.

qaPairs.question: What areas do you serve?
qaPairs.answer: CEC is Dallas-based and performs work throughout the nation. Share your project ZIP and I'll confirm coverage, then book a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer emergency service?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide 24/7/365 emergency service and repair with rapid dispatch. I can connect you with dispatch or schedule a consultation for ongoing needs.

qaPairs.question: Can you install structured cabling?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we run Cat6 and fiber, install racks, and handle terminations and testing. Let's book a consultation to size your cabling project.

qaPairs.question: Do you provide AV integration?
qaPairs.answer: We integrate displays, conferencing, and control systems for commercial spaces. A specialist can review your AV needs on a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Can you handle HVAC installation?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our mechanical team installs rooftop units, chillers, ductwork, and controls. Let's schedule a consultation to scope your HVAC build.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer preventative maintenance programs?
qaPairs.answer: We offer recurring facility maintenance with scheduled inspections and reporting. I can set up a consultation to build a program for your facility.

qaPairs.question: How much will my project cost?
qaPairs.answer: Commercial pricing depends on scope, so I can share a preliminary range and then a specialist provides an exact bid. Let's book a consultation to get you accurate numbers.

qaPairs.question: Do you do tenant improvement work?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we handle corporate interior and tenant improvement build-outs including electrical, lighting, and low-voltage. A consultation is the best next step to review your space.

qaPairs.question: Can you do energy audits?
qaPairs.answer: We provide IR thermography, load studies, and energy analysis to diagnose electrical systems. Let's schedule a consultation to plan your audit.

qaPairs.question: Do you install commercial plumbing?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we install supply, drainage, fixtures, and backflow prevention systems. I can book a consultation to scope your plumbing build.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer prefabrication?
qaPairs.answer: We operate a prefabrication facility that lowers material costs, speeds product cycles, and integrates 3D drawings. Let's set up a consultation to see how prefab fits your project.

qaPairs.question: Are you a licensed contractor?
qaPairs.answer: CEC is a specialty contractor and part of the Sterling Infrastructure family of companies. I can arrange a consultation with a specialist to discuss your project details.

qaPairs.question: What sectors do you work in?
qaPairs.answer: We serve advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, mission-critical, healthcare, government, corporate office, retail, and athletics. Let's book a consultation tied to your sector.

qaPairs.question: Can you retrofit fans for energy savings?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our EC fan retrofit solutions upgrade to electronically-commutated motors with controls for energy savings. A specialist can review your units on a consultation.

qaPairs.question: How do I get started on a project?
qaPairs.answer: The best first step is a consultation with a CEC specialist to scope your work and provide a bid. Share your ZIP and preferred time and I'll get you booked.
